data.content_ref: inline:The target's account fails because it uses a binary model of survival ('the only surviving variant') to justify a graded preference ('best-corroborated'). In actual scientific practice, multiple theories often survive the same ecosystem of tests. When more than one theory is 'left standing', the binary survival metric provides no basis for preferring one over the other, defeating the target's attempt to defend the preference for the 'best' theory. Conversely, if 'best-corroborated' is taken to imply a comparative degree of fitness to break the tie, the analogy smuggles back the very graded, predictive notion of fitness ('prediction of future dominance') that the target explicitly rejects. Thus, the account either fails to guide preference among multiple survivors, or it contradicts its own anti-inductive constraints.
